contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you chose your issue. Today: research who actually has the authority to act on it!

Real civic action requires knowing exactly which level and branch of government (or which local body, like a school board) has authority over your issue — connecting directly back to last week's government-structure content. A school-related issue might be a school board matter, a street-safety issue might be a city council matter, and a state-law issue might be a state legislature matter. Using last week's knowledge of government structure, identify which level or body most likely has authority over your chosen civic issue, and explain your reasoning.
You just identified who has real authority over your issue! Tomorrow we'll develop your action plan.

objectives: Apply last week's government-structure knowledge to identify who has authority over the chosen issue
Explain the reasoning behind the identified level/body of authority
materialsNeeded: Yesterday's worksheet, last week's government-structure notes
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's issue-choice work and last week's government-structure content.
2. Introduce identifying the correct level/body of authority using the school-board/city-council/state examples.
3. Have the child identify authority for their own issue.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's action-plan lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: work through the three example categories (school, city, state) together and ask which one the child's issue most resembles
Ready for more: ask the child what might happen if they contacted the WRONG level of government about their issue, and why getting this right matters
This is a genuine application of last week's government-structure content — the child sees why understanding government's structure has real practical value
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended activity — check that the child's identified level/body of authority genuinely matches their chosen issue's nature (a school issue to a school board, a local issue to a city council, etc.) and that their reasoning connects back to real government-structure knowledge from last week.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses this course's capstone-civics-project and how-government-works threads together, connecting last week's structural knowledge to this week's real action-planning.
